LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 GENDER NEUTRAL LANGUAGE

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can one avoid gender bias in communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts
2. use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts
   In simple words: practise until you can identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences
   In simple words: practise until you can use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language in the examples.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
4. Show that you can: identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Listen to common English songs and pick out gender biased words and phrases,
2. Read sections of a poem or story and pick out words with gender bias,
3. Critical thinking and problem solving: It is enhanced as the learner analyses concepts by logical reasoning to fill in a crossword puzzle featuring gender neutral words/phrases. Values:
4. Unity: It is enhanced as the learner cooperates with peers when participating in group tasks.
5. Self-efficacy: It is enhanced as the learner shows concerted attention when forming different types of sentences using gender 7

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can one avoid gender bias in communication?
2. Which words demonstrate gender sensitivity in communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify gender biased words and phrases in oral and written texts
2. use gender neutral words and phrases in sentences

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
